paragraphs: R. Yehudah ben Nekosa, Rabbi's student. Rabbi and R. Chiyya were traveling, with R. Yehudah ben Kenosa walking before them. Rabbi asked, “Who displays greatness before us?” R. Chiyya said, “Perhaps it is R. Yehudah ben Kenosa, his student, whose deeds are all for Heaven's sake.” [In the checked Bavli, Chiyya says “my student.”] Reaching him, he said, “Were you not Yehudah ben Kenosa, I would cut your legs with iron shears”—meaning a ban: Merubbah, Bava Kamma 81b. R. Yehudah ben Nekosa explained before Rabbi: Bava Batra 71a. In R. Yaakov's name: Chullin 118b, near the end. He reported a ruling in Sumkhos’s name in Bava Kamma 39b. Both appear separately in Yoma 18a, where Sumkhos speaks in Rabbi Meir’s name. Kohelet Midrash, on “All things are wearying”: R. Yehudah ben Nekosa—the text there is erroneous—defeated the sectarians and crushed their brains. They bewitched him: a vessel of precious stones he had became coals. In R. Shimon's name: Tosefta Negaim, chapter 4. Yalkut, Tazria, on “He shall shave”: ben Nakuv in R. Shimon's name. I found written R. Yehudah ben Nekuva in R. Shimon's name; perhaps it should read ben Nekosa.
